$comment: Registry of external sources referenced by the skill. Every id must be documented in skills/anti-ai-design/references/reference-library.md (enforced by npm run validate:references). Verification statuses are defined in references/source-verification.md. 'reachable' means HTTP success with the expected page title; it does not mean the content supports any claim.

sources.name: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
sources.learn: Testable success criteria for contrast, keyboard, focus, target size, reflow, errors, authentication.
sources.caveats: Normative for web content; applied to native apps by analogy and by some regulations. Success criteria levels (A/AA/AAA) matter for compliance claims.

sources.name: Understanding WCAG 2.2
sources.learn: Intent, examples, and techniques behind each success criterion.
sources.caveats: Informative, not normative.

sources.name: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI)
sources.learn: Entry point to WAI standards, tutorials, and evaluation resources.
sources.caveats: Hub page; cite specific resources rather than the home page.

sources.name: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG)
sources.learn: Keyboard models and ARIA roles/states for custom widgets (tabs, menus, comboboxes, grids, dialogs).
sources.caveats: Patterns are examples; test with assistive technology. Prefer native elements first.

sources.name: MDN Web Docs: Accessibility
sources.learn: Practical HTML/ARIA/CSS accessibility techniques and browser support.
sources.caveats: Community-maintained reference; verify browser support tables for new features.

sources.name: MDN: prefers-reduced-motion
sources.learn: The CSS media feature for honoring reduced-motion user preferences.
sources.caveats: Reference for the API, not for which animations to reduce.

sources.name: web.dev: Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS)
sources.learn: How layout shift is measured and avoided (dimensions on media, reserved space).
sources.caveats: Google-authored; metric thresholds may change over time.

sources.name: Apple Human Interface Guidelines
sources.learn: Apple's platform conventions, components, materials, accessibility, and patterns.
sources.caveats: Updated frequently (current guidance describes Liquid Glass). Pages are client-rendered; cite specific pages and dates.

sources.name: Apple HIG: Accessibility
sources.learn: Control sizes per platform, contrast table, Dynamic Type, motion and transparency settings.
sources.caveats: Numbers are recommendations for Apple platforms.

verification.notes: Read via Apple's documentation JSON. Control size table: iOS/iPadOS default 44x44 pt, minimum 28x28 pt; macOS default 28x28 pt, minimum 20x20 pt. Contrast table: 4.5:1 up to 17 pt; 3:1 at 18 pt or bold.

sources.name: Apple HIG: Designing for macOS
sources.learn: Mac device characteristics and best practices: large displays with less nesting and modality, resizable windows, the menu bar, high-precision input, keyboard shortcuts, personalization.
sources.caveats: High-level; follow links to component pages for specifics.

sources.name: Apple HIG: Designing for iOS
sources.learn: iPhone characteristics and best practices: limit onscreen controls, adapt to orientation, Dark Mode and Dynamic Type, place controls within reach, swipe to go back.
sources.caveats: High-level; follow links for component specifics.

sources.name: Apple HIG: Materials
sources.learn: Liquid Glass as a functional layer for controls and navigation above content; don't use it in the content layer; use sparingly; standard materials for the content layer.
sources.caveats: Apple-platform semantics; not a license for decorative glass on the web.

sources.name: Apple HIG: Motion
sources.learn: Add motion purposefully; make motion optional; brief and precise feedback; avoid motion on frequent interactions; let people cancel motion.
sources.caveats: No timing values are specified; timing guidance in this skill is our own starting point.

sources.name: Apple HIG: Sidebars
sources.learn: No more than two levels of hierarchy; let people hide the sidebar; avoid critical items at the bottom on macOS; consider a tab bar first on iOS/iPadOS.
sources.caveats: Change log shows a June 8, 2026 update; re-check before citing details.

sources.name: Apple HIG: Dark Mode
sources.learn: Respect the system appearance; avoid app-specific appearance settings; test with Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency.
sources.caveats: Apple platforms; web apps commonly offer a theme toggle, which is a different context.

sources.name: Apple HIG: Buttons
sources.learn: Hit regions of at least 44x44 pt as a general rule (60x60 pt in visionOS); button placement conventions.
sources.caveats: Platform-specific sections differ; read the relevant one.

sources.name: Apple (apple.com)
sources.learn: Product-led marketing composition: large product imagery, short statements, pacing across a long page.
sources.caveats: Depends on world-class photography and a famous brand; principles transfer, budgets and assets often do not. Do not copy compositions or assets. Content not inspected in detail this session.

sources.name: Linear
sources.learn: Real product interface used as the main visual across sections (workspace, backlog, timeline, code review views).
sources.caveats: Its homepage, as inspected, also contains a three-column icon card row and testimonial cards: a reminder that references are not anti-pattern-free and that principles matter more than pages. Do not copy its dark aesthetic as a default (GEN-008).

verification.notes: Automated fetch and summary of homepage structure; marketing pages change often.

sources.name: Stripe
sources.learn: Evidence-led storytelling with concrete metrics and named customer case studies.
sources.caveats: As inspected (a localized French version was served), the homepage uses an animated wave background, logo carousels, and several card groups; metrics are Stripe's own claims. Learn the evidence principle, not the gradient.

verification.notes: Automated fetch and summary of homepage structure.

sources.name: Raycast
sources.learn: Demonstrating a keyboard-first product through keyboard visuals and real UI screenshots of the launcher, AI chat, and extensions.
sources.caveats: Marketing page for a developer-leaning audience; patterns may not suit other audiences.

verification.notes: Automated fetch and summary of homepage structure.

sources.name: Mobbin
sources.learn: How shipped apps handle specific flows (onboarding, paywalls, settings, empty states).
sources.caveats: Commercial service; much content requires an account or subscription. Screenshots belong to the depicted products: study, don't reproduce. Popular patterns are not necessarily good ones.

sources.name: shadcn/ui
sources.learn: Open-code component distribution: components are copied into the project so they can be fully customized; it describes itself as 'not a component library' but a way to build one.
sources.caveats: Default styling is widely used, so unmodified defaults read as generic. Apply the project's art direction to the copied components.

sources.name: Material Design 3
sources.learn: Google's design system: components, color system (including dynamic color), typography, layout and adaptive guidance.
sources.caveats: Client-rendered site; specific deep links change (one tested deep link returned 404 on 2026-10-19). Cite pages after opening them. Not every Android app must look like Material.

sources.name: Android Developers: Design & Plan
sources.learn: Android design entry point linking platform, layout, and quality guidance.
sources.caveats: Hub page.

sources.name: Android Developers: Make apps more accessible
sources.learn: 48x48 dp minimum touch targets; 4.5:1 contrast for small text and 3:1 otherwise; sp units for text; content descriptions.
sources.caveats: Examples use Jetpack Compose; Views equivalents exist.

sources.name: Android Developers: Use window size classes
sources.learn: Width classes: compact <600 dp, medium 600-840, expanded 840-1200, large 1200-1600, extra-large >=1600; height classes compact <480, medium 480-900, expanded >=900.
sources.caveats: Large and extra-large classes require opting in via the adaptive library API.

sources.name: Android Developers: Get started with adaptive apps
sources.learn: Adaptive app guidance for phones, foldables, tablets, desktop windows.
sources.caveats: Compose-focused.

sources.name: Android Developers: Dynamic color
sources.learn: Letting users' wallpaper-derived colors personalize the app's palette.
sources.caveats: Views page; availability depends on Android version and device.

sources.name: Microsoft Fluent 2 Design System
sources.learn: Microsoft's cross-platform design system, with resources for web (React), iOS, Android, and Windows.
sources.caveats: Homepage inspected only; read specific foundation pages before citing details.

sources.name: Microsoft Learn: Design Windows apps
sources.learn: Windows app design guidance: layout, controls, navigation, input.
informs: Windows conventions for cross-platform desktop apps
sources.caveats: Hub page.

sources.name: Nielsen Norman Group
sources.learn: Research-informed UX articles on navigation, forms, IA, usability testing, and more.
sources.caveats: Secondary source; articles vary in age and method. Cite specific articles with dates.

sources.name: NN/g: 10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design
sources.learn: Ten heuristics including visibility of system status, consistency and standards, error prevention, recognition rather than recall.
sources.caveats: Heuristics guide expert review; they don't replace user research.

verification.notes: Heuristic names confirmed; page shows last update 30 January 2024.

sources.name: Electron documentation
sources.learn: Web-technology desktop apps: menus, native dialogs, window APIs.
informs: what native integration is available in Electron
sources.caveats: Check API availability per OS.

sources.name: Tauri
sources.learn: Desktop (and mobile) apps with a system webview and a Rust core; native menus and dialogs.
sources.caveats: System webviews differ per OS (rendering and feature support).

sources.name: Qt Documentation
sources.learn: Qt Widgets and Qt Quick, styles, and platform integration.
sources.caveats: Version-specific; check the documentation for the Qt version in use.

sources.name: Flutter: Adaptive and responsive design
sources.learn: Adapting Flutter apps across form factors and input types.
sources.caveats: Flutter renders its own widgets; native look requires deliberate work.

sources.name: Agent Skills specification
sources.learn: SKILL.md frontmatter rules: name 1-64 chars, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens, no leading/trailing/consecutive hyphens, must match the directory; description 1-1024 chars; optional license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools.
sources.caveats: Individual products may support additional fields or apply stricter limits.

sources.name: Claude Code Docs: Extend Claude with skills
sources.learn: Personal skills in ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, project skills in .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, plugin skills in <plugin>/skills/<name>/; supporting files linked from SKILL.md load on demand; keep SKILL.md under 500 lines.
sources.caveats: Claude Code-specific frontmatter fields are not portable.

sources.name: Claude Platform Docs: Agent Skills overview
sources.learn: Agent Skills on the Claude API and apps.
sources.caveats: Reachability checked only.

sources.name: Claude Help Center: Use skills in Claude
sources.learn: Upload a ZIP of the skill folder in Customize > Skills; requires code execution to be enabled.
sources.caveats: Plan availability and UI paths change; re-check before documenting to users.

sources.name: OpenAI: Build skills (Codex)
sources.learn: Codex scans $CWD/.agents/skills, $REPO_ROOT/.agents/skills, $HOME/.agents/skills, /etc/codex/skills, and bundled skills; invoke with /skills or by typing $ to mention a skill.
sources.caveats: developers.openai.com/codex/skills redirected here (308) on 2026-10-19.

sources.name: OpenAI Academy: Skills
sources.learn: ChatGPT skills use the SKILL.md format; can be built in ChatGPT or uploaded; selected automatically or by @-mentioning; exportable to other Agent Skills tools such as Codex.
sources.caveats: Does not state plan availability, accepted upload formats, or size limits.

sources.name: OpenAI Help Center: Skills in ChatGPT
sources.learn: Skills are available to eligible ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu users, subject to workspace settings; upload via Skills > Create > Upload from your computer; uploads are scanned and may be marked Needs Review or Blocked; skills can be shared with a workspace.
sources.caveats: The page text inspected does not list accepted upload file formats or size limits. curl and some fetchers received HTTP 403; Node fetch received the page.

verification.notes: Page text retrieved with Node fetch and read.

sources.name: Impeccable: Slop catalog
sources.learn: Named catalog of patterns that expose AI-generated UI: side-tab accent borders, grid-line backgrounds, italic serif display headlines, hero metric layouts, numbered section labels, pulsing dots, marquees, em-dash overuse, forced 'not X but Y' contrast, cream/beige palettes.
sources.caveats: Opinionated list from a commercial design tool; a listed pattern is a tell, not a defect in every context.

verification.notes: Page text read; about 67 patterns listed under Your design system, Visual Details, Typography, Color & Contrast, Layout & Space, Motion, Copy, Imagery, General quality.

sources.name: Anthropic: Improving frontend design through Skills
sources.learn: Unguided models converge on Inter fonts, purple gradients on white backgrounds, and minimal animations; advises avoiding generic fonts like Arial and Inter and clichéd purple gradients.
sources.caveats: Written to promote a skill; its recommendations can harden into new defaults.

verification.notes: Article dated 2025-11-12; quoted passages on fonts, colors, and layouts read.

sources.name: How to tell if a website is vibe coded
sources.learn: Signs of unreviewed generated sites: purple gradient heroes, three-column feature cards, emoji in headings, glowing hovers, upbeat microcopy, placeholder testimonials, builder badges, dead buttons, forms without feedback.
sources.caveats: Blog post; anecdotal, no data.

verification.notes: Page text read; UI, copy, builder-marker, and interactivity sections summarized.
